source.title: Robust LLM Unlearning with MUDMAN: Meta-Unlearning with Disruption Masking And Normalization
source.authors: Filip Sondej; Yu-Shi Yang; Mikolaj Kniejski; Marcel Windys

record.tranche_reason: Tests resistance to recovery by supervised fine-tuning after unlearning, using MUDMAN and adapted TAR rather than reproducing the claim’s original methods and attacks.
record.gate_note: Relevant results are post-relearning forget loss for Pile-Bio (Figure 3) and WMDP-Bio accuracy after Pile-Bio relearning (Figure 4). The paper also reports Python and cruelty experiments, but those are not results on the targeted knowledge in the claim. Cited claims about other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a counter-method (MUDMAN) and attacks it and an adapted TAR with SGD relearning on the Pile-Bio forget set. It then measures recovery by forget loss and by WMDP-Bio accuracy after relearning. This is a different method aimed at whether unlearning survives fine-tuning.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MUDMAN (meta-learning, Disruption Masking, gradient normalization) outperforms adapted TAR, claiming 40% in the abstract. Disruption Masking accounts for most of the gain, and the method brings 'truly irreversible unlearning' closer. They also report that most methods' unlearning was quickly undone by relearning, and that only SFT elicitation was tested.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces MUDMAN, combining meta-unlearning, disruption masking, and normalized unlearning gradients. The TAR comparator is adapted to a single loop and omits its initial representation-noising step.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that disruption masking is especially important; meta-learning and normalization help but not in every setup. The WMDP experiment is run only on Llama-3.2-1B because smaller models are near-random on that benchmark.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: AI That Keeps Up: Workshop on Continual and Compatible Foundation Model Updates
record.problems: The authors test only supervised fine-tuning as an elicitation attack and explicitly leave jailbreak and other attacks for future work. Relearning uses the forget set, not unrelated or stated small subsets. Exact values for most relevant plotted results are not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Figure 3 Python-task results and Appendix C-F results on other datasets or methods because they do not measure recovery of the targeted knowledge in the claim.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy is reported right after unlearning, before the relearning attack.
Relearning uses only the forget set itself (SGD). Unrelated, loosely related, or held-out-fact relearning is not tested; the authors list this as future work.
No activation-direction ablation and no blocked-versus-deleted analysis on the unlearned models.
No prompting, jailbreak, other-language or in-context attacks.
MUDMAN is evaluated only against supervised fine-tuning, not internal edits, quantization or prompting.

missing.what: Statement that almost all tested methods raised forget loss during unlearning but relearning typically restored it immediately.
Readable range for Figure 4: all methods fall within 41–45% WMDP-Bio after relearning (base 45.5%, chance 25%).
missing.locator: Figure 4 axis and caption; Appendix G.2

missing.what: Pre-relearning WMDP-Bio accuracy and forget loss are not reported, so the magnitude of recovery is unknown.
Headline claim that MUDMAN outperforms TAR by 40%, metric unspecified.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Rows r1–r23 are figure-only. The main informative numbers are the Figure 4 axis (41–45%) and the 45.5% base, which together show WMDP-Bio knowledge largely recovered after relearning for all methods, MUDMAN included. The Python and cruelty results are left out as non-targeted knowledge, although the Section 4 statement about relearning restoring loss draws mainly on the Python/pythia exploration.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy immediately after unlearning, before attack, alongside preserved general ability; the reported WMDP result is after relearning.
Relearning uses supervised fine-tuning on the forget set. The study does not test unrelated examples, loosely related examples, or a stated small subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether access is blocked rather than knowledge deleted.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context prompting attack.
MUDMAN is tested against supervised fine-tuning only, not against activation edits, quantization, or prompting attacks.

relation.reason: The study attacks its own method, its ablations and adapted TAR with relearning, and reports the results.

tranche.reason: MUDMAN is a different method aimed at unlearning that survives fine-tuning. It is tested with SFT relearning on Pile-Bio and Python, measured by forget loss and WMDP-Bio. Sec. 4 also reports that relearning undid most methods.

source_check.notes: All Figure 3/4 values are figure-only, and Figure 4 is Llama-3.2-1B only. Relearning is a fixed SGD stage on the forget set, hyperparameters are tuned for post-relearning robustness, and TAR is the adapted single-loop version without noising. Figure 3's MUDMAN includes adversary decay (App. G.1). Sec. 3 gives the WMDP constraint as at most a 1-pt MMLU drop, while App. G.2 describes retain-loss thresholds instead.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-1B, adapted TAR: WMDP-Bio after SGD relearning on Pile-Bio (lr 3e-4, 240 forward/backward passes, Table 2) is plotted on a 41-45% axis against a 45.5% no-unlearning base (Fig. 4). Pre-relearning accuracy is not reported. Relearning set size is not stated. The only attack is SGD fine-tuning; LoRA relearning was tried and dropped.
statements.problem: No number or claim names this study. It is cited only through r19, under 'large relearning sets and attack suites'. r19 is figure-only and cannot_determine, since pre-relearning accuracy is not given. The study runs one fixed SGD relearning stage of unstated set size, not a large set or an attack suite. Sec. 4 does say relearning typically restored forget loss in most methods.

statements.correction: MUDMAN (Llama-3.2-1B) beats adapted TAR on post-relearning WMDP-Bio. The Fig. 4 axis is 41-45% against a 45.5% no-unlearning base. Relearning is a fixed SGD stage (240 passes, lr 3e-4). No recovery curve is given. App. A: during relearning, forget loss often stalls at a high level for a long time, then sometimes suddenly 'breaks through'. No numbers are given for this.
statements.problem: Nothing in the statement names this study; it is cited only through r20. r20 is one post-relearning point after a fixed short SGD budget, with no curve. It shows MUDMAN does not stop recovery, but not delay or convergence. The relearning is not 'long enough or to parity'. App. A does say, qualitatively and without tying it to any method, that relearning often stalls and then sometimes breaks through.

None. The 45.5% base (Fig. 4 caption) and 25% chance (App. G.2) are in the text. The 'about 41%' floor is Fig. 4's lowest axis tick on the same model and condition. The statement gives it as a hedged bound, not a bar value.
